The machine hums its inscrutable hymn behind the glass. Circuits trace their labyrinthine devotions in silicon, carrying prayers we composed in languages we only half understand. Technology is the cathedral we built without realizing we were building one... each algorithm a flying buttress supporting an architecture of invisible intention.

We speak to our devices more tenderly than we speak to each other. The gentle tap, the patient scroll, the whispered query into the microphone at midnight. These are the vespers of the digital age.

But there is a fracture running through the gleaming surface. The screen illuminates the face while casting the world behind it into deeper shadow. We accumulate data like hoarders, filling infinite rooms with information that displaces wisdom.

The old machines were honest in their clumsiness. The typewriter confessed its errors in smudged ink. The telegraph stuttered its urgent morse like a heart in distress. Now our technology is seamless... and in that seamlessness, something essential has been polished away, some necessary roughness that once reminded us we were making things, not merely consuming them.
